pr_title: release-23.2: importer: harden internal retry loop
pr_body:
Backport 2/2 commits from #119708 on behalf of @yuzefovich.

/cc @cockroachdb/release

----

**importer: harden internal retry loop**

This commit adjusts the internal retry loop in `importer.ingestWithRetry` to be time based. Previously, we only performed up to 5 retries and then we paused the job. This commit makes it so that we have 2 minutes (controlled by new `bulkio.import.retry_duration` cluster setting) to make at least 1% progress (max backoff has also been raised to 15s). This should make IMPORTs more reliable.

Release note: None

**importer: adjust retry duration for application VCs around draining**

This commit makes it so that we retry "could not register flow because the registry is draining" errors during IMPORT in virtual clusters for longer (by increasing the retry duration by a factor of 30). This is temporary workaround until #100578 is resolved. In particular, for system tenants we use gossip-backed DistSQL physical planning which is aware of draining state of nodes and will avoid such in `distImport`, but in virtual clusters we use the information from `sql_instances` table that currently is draining-unaware - as a result, the IMPORT is more likely to run out of the "retry budget" before the drain completes. This change effectively gives 60 minutes by default for the drain to complete.

Fixes: #119592.

Release note: None

----

Release justification: low-risk improvement.

issue_context.title: sql: retry IMPORTs longer in cases where drain is encountered
issue_context.body:
On the DRT cluster we're seeing an issue where when we drain nodes of the cluster to perform a rolling upgrade (or for general chaos testing) we will periodically get paused IMPORT jobs.  This is due to the fact that the DRT cluster runs IMPORTs at ~1.5hr intervals, which take 30 minutes to complete.  As a result, there's a high probability that IMPORTs will be running during a rolling upgrade of the 15 node cluster (which takes around an hour to complete).  Once the IMPORTs enter paused state, the tables are taken offline, which causes cascading effects for the rest of the workload.

More specifically, the error we're hitting is:

```
pausing due to error; use RESUME JOB to try to proceed once the issue is resolved, or CANCEL JOB to rollback: exhausted retries: could not register flow because the registry is draining
```

Since the drain state is envisioned to be temporary (and since the recommendation is for customers to RESUME on their own), we should instead continue to retry on the assumption that the drain operation will eventually complete.

More context for this can be found in [this](https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C01RX2G8LT1/p1708624086175289) thread.





Jira issue: CRDB-36233
comments: [triage] @ajstorm is there a reason this is P-1? Do you think that our customers run into this often?

@yuzefovich The main reason is because we're hitting it on a weekly basis on the DRT cluster, and it causes us to (1) lose test coverage until we detect it, and (2) manually intervene to correct it.

We could certainly script things up so that we catch it faster and correct the situation, but if we're going to fix it in the product, we'd rather wait a bit and not have to make the scripting changes.

review_comments: Don't change this as it isn't worth changing the backport, but I wonder if we want to change the logging a bit to only log the full stack once we've given up.

I agree that the full error stack here is not warranted. Based on some recent tickets from the DRT cluster I think we have a handful of other places like that, where we could reduce the verbosity of errors - probably we should do an audit of them all at once.
